plain.text: Another large crowd had been with Jesus for three days with nothing to eat. Jesus had compassion on them. The disciples had seven loaves and a few small fish. Jesus gave thanks, broke the bread, and the disciples handed it out. About four thousand people ate and were satisfied, and seven baskets of leftovers were collected.
The Pharisees came and argued with Jesus, asking for a sign from heaven to test him. He sighed deeply and said no sign would be given to this generation. Then he left them.

In the boat, the disciples had forgotten to bring bread. Jesus warned them, "Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and of Herod." They thought he was talking about having no bread. Jesus reminded them how much was left over when he fed the five thousand and the four thousand, and asked, "Do you still not understand?"

At Bethsaida, people brought a blind man to Jesus. Jesus led him out of the village, put spit on his eyes and laid his hands on him. The man said, "I see people, but they look like trees walking around." Jesus touched his eyes again, and he saw everything clearly.

On the way to the villages near Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked, "Who do people say I am?" They said John the Baptist, Elijah, or one of the prophets. "But what about you?" he asked. "Who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Christ." Jesus warned them not to tell anyone.

Then Jesus began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the leaders, be killed, and after three days rise again. He said this plainly. Peter took him aside and began to scold him. Jesus turned and rebuked Peter: "Get behind me, Satan! You are thinking like people, not like God."

Jesus called the crowd and said, "Whoever wants to follow me must deny themselves, take up their cross and follow me. Whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me and the good news will save it. What good is it to gain the whole world but lose your soul?"

summary.bigIdea: Peter recognises Jesus as the Christ, and Jesus explains that the Christ must suffer, die and rise.
points: Jesus feeds four thousand, but even his disciples are slow to understand.
A blind man's sight comes back in two stages, as the disciples' understanding does.
Following Jesus means taking up your cross and losing your life to find it.
summary.reflection: Jesus asks, "Who do you say I am?" How would you answer today?
